boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of San Diego, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that starts with campus orientation and mixes landmarks, study space, food, art, and a student event.

cards.title: Start by getting oriented
cards.subtitle: New Student Programs • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Use the orientation hub to confirm your assigned sessions, then introduce yourself to one person before heading out to explore campus.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the university’s new-student onboarding program.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes undergraduate orientation as including sessions, workshops, social events, and exploration of campus opportunities.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Student Orientation — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: Follow the orientation program’s instructions for assigned activities.

cards.title: Get your campus bearings at The Immaculata
cards.subtitle: 5998 Alcalá Park • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Walk to the blue-domed church, pause outside to orient yourself, and check the posted church hours before going inside.
cards.short_summary: A prominent campus landmark with regularly posted church hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Immaculata is located on USD’s campus at 5998 Alcalá Park, and its site publishes church hours and Mass times.
cards.access_notes: Church hours are listed as 8:30 a.m.–6 p.m. daily; services may affect quiet access.

cards.title: Cross through Colachis Plaza
cards.subtitle: Between Hughes Administration Center and The Immaculata
cards.notes: Use this central plaza as a walking checkpoint, then look for the fountain area before continuing toward the older campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named central plaza beside The Immaculata.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s campus-space directory lists Colachis Plaza between Hughes Administration Center and The Immaculata.
cards.source_title: Signature Spaces and Plazas — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; observe any event setup or access notices.

cards.title: See the history inside Founders Chapel
cards.subtitle: Behind Founders Hall • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Take the official virtual or in-person tour option, or stop by during open worship times to see the chapel’s art and architecture.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus chapel with tours and recurring services.
cards.evidence_claim: USD states that Founders Chapel is behind Founders Hall, offers tours, and serves as the main chapel for university Masses.
cards.source_title: Founders Chapel Tours — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: Tours and services have separate schedules; check the official page before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Helen K. and James S. Copley Library
cards.title: Claim a calm hour at Copley Library
cards.subtitle: Camino Hall • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Find the main study areas and the Mother Rosalie Hill Reading Room, then save the library page for research help later in the term.
cards.short_summary: A campus library stop for settling in and finding study space.
cards.evidence_claim: USD identifies Copley Library in Camino Hall and describes its main study areas, reading room, and Special Collections and Archives.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current access and service hours before planning a study session.

cards.title: Take a quiet loop through Garden of the Sea
cards.subtitle: Plaza and garden • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Use the campus map to locate this named garden, then make it a short outdoor reset between the library and your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A named campus garden for a brief outdoor pause.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s campus map lists Garden of the Sea among its plazas and gardens.
cards.source_title: University of San Diego Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; use the current campus map and follow any posted access guidance.

cards.entity_name: Fine Art Galleries at the Joan B. Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice
cards.title: Check what’s showing at the Kroc galleries
cards.subtitle: Joan B. Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice • USD
cards.notes: Look for the Fine Art Galleries in the Kroc Institute, and pair the stop with a walk around the building’s east courtyard.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery stop in the Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s campus map lists Fine Art Galleries in the Joan B. Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice.
cards.source_title: University of San Diego Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Exhibition availability and gallery access can vary; confirm on site before planning a visit.

cards.title: Take a meal break at La Paloma
cards.subtitle: Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice • USD
cards.notes: Choose a made-to-order meal or drink, then use the indoor or outdoor seating to regroup before the afternoon’s campus activities.
cards.short_summary: A Kroc Institute dining venue with mobile ordering and varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: USD says La Paloma is in the Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice and offers made-to-order food, espresso and tea, plus indoor and outdoor seating.
cards.source_title: La Paloma — University of San Diego Dining
cards.access_notes: Current hours are published by USD Dining; food and drinks require payment.

cards.title: Find your way around Pavilion Dining
cards.subtitle: Student Life Pavilion • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Walk through the Student Life Pavilion food court, note the dining concepts, and meet up with classmates for a straightforward dinner plan.
cards.short_summary: A Student Life Pavilion food court with multiple dining concepts.
cards.evidence_claim: USD identifies Pavilion Dining in the Student Life Pavilion as a food court with multiple dining concepts.
cards.access_notes: All campus eateries are described as open to students and visitors; verify current dining hours.

cards.title: End with a Torero Program Board event
cards.subtitle: Student-led campus programming • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Check the current event listings and choose an age-appropriate concert, cultural program, speaker, or recreation event that fits your evening.
cards.short_summary: Student-led programming provides recurring campus-event options.
cards.evidence_claim: USD says the student-led Torero Program Board plans campus events including concerts, cultural events, speakers, and athletic tailgates.
cards.source_title: Clubs and Organizations — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: Offerings, entry requirements, and costs vary by event; consult the current official listing.
